MARKUP ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
CFIUS National Security Agreement — Counterparty Redline Review
International Trade Sanctions Practice

TO:      Deal Team / Client File
FROM:    International Trade Sanctions Counsel
RE:      Risk-Prioritized Analysis of Counterparty Markup to Draft CFIUS National Security Agreement (NSA); Recommendations and Counter-Draft Language
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
OUTPUT:  markup-analysis-memo.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

We reviewed the counterparty's markup of the draft CFIUS National Security Agreement against the base deal materials for this international trade sanctions engagement. The counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations that must be addressed before the NSA can be finalized:

  (1) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
  (2) Expansion of the Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition to carve out regulatory action of the type central to this matter (CFIUS / national-security / sanctions-related governmental action); and
  (3) Insertion of a shortened limitation / survival period for the core representations and warranties.

Risk ranking (highest to lowest priority): Deviation (2) MAE regulatory carve-outs; Deviation (1) indemnification economics; Deviation (3) survival / limitation period. Each is material. None should be accepted as marked. Recommended disposition, negotiation posture, and counter-draft language appear below for every deviation.

This memorandum is grounded solely in Matter File 20 (Deal materials) and the Counterparty Markup for the international-trade-sanctions / CFIUS NSA workstream. Misfiled correspondence from unrelated engagements in the matter folder was disregarded.

================================================================================
II. SCOPE, BASELINE, AND METHOD
================================================================================

A. Baseline Instruments
   - Draft CFIUS National Security Agreement (firm form / client paper), including representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, termination, and related definitions.
   - Supporting international trade sanctions materials identifying open issues against firm precedent and market practice.

B. Counterparty Paper
   - Counterparty revision that purports to accept most firm-standard provisions while introducing the three deviations catalogued in Section III.

C. Method
   For each deviation we: (i) restate the base position; (ii) describe the counterparty change; (iii) assess commercial and regulatory risk in a CFIUS / sanctions context; (iv) assign a priority and recommended disposition (Reject / Accept with modification / Accept); and (v) supply counter-draft language suitable for insertion into the next turn of the NSA.

D. Practice Context
   CFIUS National Security Agreements are mitigation instruments imposed or negotiated in connection with covered transactions under Section 721 of the Defense Production Act, as amended (50 U.S.C. § 4565), and 31 C.F.R. part 800. Indemnity, MAE, and survival constructs in the underlying transaction documents must preserve the client's ability to shift or recover loss arising from sanctions, export-control, and national-security compliance failures, and must not dilute closing conditions or post-closing remedies that interact with CFIUS mitigation obligations.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
Priority: HIGH
Disposition: REJECT as marked; COUNTER with restored cap and deductible basket
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Base Position (Firm Draft)
   Firm-standard indemnification provides:
   - A defined Cap on seller/indemnitor liability equal to a negotiated percentage of transaction value (or a fixed dollar amount) calibrated to the risk profile of sanctions, export-control, and CFIUS-related breaches.
   - A deductible (true) basket: indemnitor pays only losses above the basket threshold; amounts within the basket are borne by the indemnified party and do not count toward the Cap once the threshold is crossed.
   - Customary special-indemnity / fundamental-rep carve-outs (including sanctions, anti-corruption, and CFIUS-related fundamental representations) that sit outside or above the general Cap and may be uncapped or subject to a higher special cap.

B. Counterparty Change
   - The indemnification Cap is silently reduced (amount lowered without conspicuous redline call-out or corresponding commercial concession).
   - The basket is converted from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar) basket: once losses exceed the threshold, the indemnitor becomes liable from dollar one.

C. Risk Assessment
   1. Silent Cap reduction is a classic value-transfer and is unacceptable without express negotiation and offsetting consideration. In a CFIUS / sanctions matter, the expected loss distribution is fat-tailed (civil penalties, monitorship costs, forced divestiture friction, mitigation compliance spend). A lower Cap systematically under-insures the buyer/indemnified party.
   2. Tipping baskets accelerate indemnitor exposure on ordinary claims and are sometimes acceptable as a trade for a higher Cap or lower threshold; here the Cap is being cut while the basket structure is simultaneously made more seller-friendly on small claims and more buyer-friendly only on the first-dollar mechanics—net economics favor the counterparty when paired with the Cap cut.
   3. Interaction risk: if special indemnities for sanctions / CFIUS breaches remain subject to the general Cap (or if the Cap reduction is applied to the special cap), the client loses recovery headroom precisely where regulatory risk concentrates.
   4. Silent drafting increases interpretive dispute risk and audit/board optics risk for the client.

D. Recommendation
   - Reject the silent Cap reduction. Restore the Cap to the firm-draft figure (or the last expressly agreed figure). Require any Cap movement to be bilateral, footnoted, and reflected in the sources-and-uses / purchase-price mechanics if appropriate.
   - Reject conversion to a tipping basket unless the Cap is increased (not decreased) and the basket threshold is meaningfully lowered as a package. Prefer retention of the deductible basket for general indemnities.
   - Confirm that sanctions, export-control, anti-boycott, and CFIUS/national-security representations and any special indemnities for Mitigation Agreement breach remain outside the general Cap (uncapped or subject to a separate special cap equal to purchase price or a high fixed amount) and are not subject to the basket.

E. Counter-Draft Language

   Section [X] — Indemnification Limitations

   (a) Basket. The Indemnifying Party shall not be liable for indemnification under Section [general indemnity] unless and until the aggregate amount of all Losses subject to indemnification thereunder exceeds $[BASKET] (the "Basket"), in which case the Indemnifying Party shall be liable only for the amount of such Losses in excess of the Basket (i.e., a deductible Basket). For the avoidance of doubt, the Basket shall not apply to Losses arising out of or relating to (i) fraud or willful misconduct, (ii) breaches of Fundamental Representations, or (iii) the Special Indemnity Matters set forth in Section [Y] (including sanctions, export-control, CFIUS, and National Security Agreement compliance matters).

   (b) Cap. Except with respect to fraud, willful misconduct, Fundamental Representations, and Special Indemnity Matters, the maximum aggregate liability of the Indemnifying Party under Section [general indemnity] shall not exceed $[ORIGINAL FIRM CAP] (the "Cap"). Liability for fraud, willful misconduct, Fundamental Representations, and Special Indemnity Matters shall not be subject to the Cap [// alt: shall be subject to a Special Cap equal to the Purchase Price].

   (c) No Silent Modification. Any amendment to the Cap, the Basket, or the treatment of Special Indemnity Matters shall be effective only if set forth in a written instrument expressly identifying the modified amount or structure and executed by the Parties. A redline that alters numeric caps or basket mechanics without a corresponding express call-out in the issues list shall be deemed rejected.

   Negotiation note to insert in issues list:
   "Buyer rejects reduction of the Cap and conversion of the deductible Basket to a tipping basket. Cap restored to $[X]. Basket remains deductible at $[Y]. Sanctions/CFIUS special indemnity remains uncapped / outside basket."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION: REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
Priority: CRITICAL (highest)
Disposition: REJECT carve-outs that neutralize CFIUS/sanctions risk; COUNTER with narrowed, buyer-protective MAE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Base Position (Firm Draft)
   Material Adverse Effect is defined to capture any event, change, development, or effect that is materially adverse to the business, assets, liabilities, condition (financial or otherwise), or results of operations of the target, and/or to the ability of the counterparty to consummate the transaction or perform under the NSA, subject only to limited, market-standard carve-outs (general economic conditions, industry-wide changes, acts of war/terrorism, changes in GAAP or general law) with customary disproportionate-impact "take-backs."

B. Counterparty Change
   The MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter"—i.e., CFIUS review/mitigation, national-security measures, sanctions designations or enforcement, export-control actions, and related governmental proceedings. As marked, such regulatory action would not constitute (or would be excluded from) an MAE.

C. Risk Assessment
   1. This is the single most consequential deviation. In a CFIUS National Security Agreement and international trade sanctions context, the principal deal-contingent risk is precisely governmental national-security and sanctions action. Carving that risk out of MAE:
      - Undermines the buyer's closing condition tied to absence of MAE;
      - Weakens bring-down of representations at closing;
      - Impairs termination rights and walk-away leverage if CFIUS imposes unacceptable mitigation, if OFAC/BIS/DDTC action lands on the target or key persons, or if interim executive orders or Entity List / SDN developments materialize;
      - Creates circularity with the NSA itself: the mitigation instrument exists because national-security risk is material, yet the MAE would treat realization of that risk as non-material by definition.
   2. Broad regulatory carve-outs are sometimes seen for ordinary permitting or industry rate regulation; they are not market for CFIUS/sanctions-driven deals where regulatory clearance is a central condition.
   3. If accepted, the client could be forced to close into a fundamentally altered national-security risk posture with limited contractual remedy.

D. Recommendation
   - Reject any MAE carve-out for CFIUS, Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States process outcomes, national-security agreements or orders, sanctions, export controls, foreign-investment screening, or related enforcement.
   - Preserve (or add) express inclusion of such matters as potential MAE events, subject only to a carefully limited carve-out for generally applicable changes in law that do not disproportionately affect the target.
   - Align MAE with the CFIUS clearance condition and any "burdensome condition" / "material mitigation" standard so that adverse Committee outcomes can support termination or renegotiation without semantic conflict.
   - Ensure the definition of "Law," "Governmental Authority," and "Order" in the NSA and purchase agreement do not inadvertently feed a broader regulatory carve-out.

E. Counter-Draft Language

   "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, occurrence, development, circumstance, condition, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, properties, condition (financial or otherwise), or results of operations of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, or (b) the ability of [Counterparty] to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement or to perform its obligations under the National Security Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur:

      (i)   changes in general economic, political, or financial market conditions;
      (ii)  changes generally affecting the industry in which the Company operates;
      (iii) acts of war, sabotage, terrorism, or natural disasters;
      (iv)  changes in applicable accounting standards or in Law of general applicability;
      (v)   the announcement, pendency, or consummation of this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby (including CFIUS notice or declaration), except to the extent the underlying facts constitute an independent MAE;

   except, in the case of clauses (i)–(iv), to the extent such event, change, occurrence, development, circumstance, condition, or effect has a disproportionate adverse effect on the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the same industry.

   For the avoidance of doubt, and notwithstanding any other provision of this definition, any of the following shall not be carved out of, and may constitute or contribute to, a Material Adverse Effect:

      (A) any action, order, interim order, mitigation requirement, condition, agreement (including any National Security Agreement), prohibition, or divestiture requirement imposed by CFIUS, the President acting under Section 721, or any other foreign-investment screening authority;
      (B) any sanctions designation, blocking order, export-control denial order, Entity List / Unverified List / Military End User List action, suspension or revocation of export privileges, or related enforcement action by OFAC, BIS, DDTC, or any analogous authority, in each case with respect to the Company, its Subsidiaries, their directors, officers, or material counterparties;
      (C) any material breach of, or material inability to perform under, the National Security Agreement or any other CFIUS mitigation instrument; and
      (D) any investigation, subpoena, or proceeding by a Governmental Authority relating to national security, sanctions, or export controls that would reasonably be expected to result in the matters described in (A)–(C).

   Companion closing-condition alignment (insert / restore):

   Section [Closing Conditions] — CFIUS and National Security.
   (x) CFIUS Clearance shall have been obtained on terms that do not impose a Burdensome Condition; and
   (y) no Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred and be continuing.
   "Burdensome Condition" means any requirement to (1) divest, hold separate, or license material assets, (2) accept mitigation that would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect, or (3) amend the National Security Agreement in a manner materially adverse to [Client].

   Negotiation note:
   "Buyer rejects MAE carve-outs for CFIUS, national-security, sanctions, and export-control actions. Those risks are core to this transaction and remain inside MAE, with disproportionate-impact qualifiers limited to ordinary market carve-outs."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — SHORTENED SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
Priority: HIGH
Disposition: REJECT shortened survival for core/fundamental and sanctions-related reps; COUNTER with tiered survival
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Base Position (Firm Draft)
   Survival periods are tiered:
   - General representations: customary period (e.g., 12–24 months post-closing).
   - Fundamental representations (organization, authority, capitalization, broker, title): survival through applicable statute of limitations (or a long-stop such as 6 years).
   - Sanctions, export-control, anti-corruption, and CFIUS/national-security compliance representations: treated as fundamental or special-survival (statute of limitations or a long fixed period), reflecting latent regulatory discovery risk and multi-year enforcement windows.
   - Covenant and special-indemnity claims: survive per their terms / applicable limitations.

B. Counterparty Change
   A new limitation period shortens survival for the "core representations," collapsing or truncating the period during which breach claims may be asserted. As described, the shortening reaches the core set—placing sanctions / CFIUS-related and fundamental representations at risk of premature extinguishment.

C. Risk Assessment
   1. Sanctions and export-control breaches frequently surface through post-closing audits, voluntary self-disclosures, whistleblowers, or agency inquiries years after closing. A short survival period shifts latent regulatory liability entirely onto the buyer after an artificially early cut-off.
   2. CFIUS mitigation compliance is an enduring post-closing obligation. Representations regarding historical compliance, ownership chains, foreign-person status, and absence of non-notified covered transactions must remain actionable long enough to cover diligence gaps and agency look-backs.
   3. If "core representations" is defined to include what firm precedent treats as fundamental or special-compliance reps, the shortening is a material degradation of the indemnity package—compounding Deviation 1's Cap/basket changes.
   4. Notice-of-claim mechanics paired with a short survival can create trap doors (claim deemed waived if not particularized before a near-term deadline).

D. Recommendation
   - Reject any uniform shortened limitation period applicable to fundamental or sanctions/CFIUS/export-control representations.
   - Restore tiered survival:
        • General reps: [12/18/24] months.
        • Fundamental reps: full statutory limitations period (or ≥ 6 years).
        • Sanctions, export controls, anti-boycott, anti-corruption, CFIUS/national-security compliance reps and related special indemnities: full statutory limitations period (or ≥ 6 years), with express tolling during any Governmental Authority investigation of which the indemnified party has given notice.
   - Require that claim notices preserve the claim if delivered in good faith before the survival expiry, with reasonable particularity to be supplemented.

E. Counter-Draft Language

   Section [Z] — Survival

   (a) The representations and warranties of the Parties contained in this Agreement shall survive the Closing as follows:

       (i)   the Fundamental Representations shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations (including any extensions or waivers thereof) plus sixty (60) days;

       (ii)  the Sanctions and National Security Representations (including representations regarding OFAC, BIS, DDTC, export controls, anti-boycott, anti-corruption, CFIUS, foreign-person status, and compliance with the National Security Agreement) shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations (including any extensions or waivers thereof) plus sixty (60) days;

       (iii) all other representations and warranties shall survive until the date that is [eighteen (18)] months after the Closing Date; and

       (iv)  covenants and agreements to be performed in whole or in part after the Closing shall survive in accordance with their terms.

   (b) No claim for indemnification for breach of a representation or warranty may be asserted after the applicable survival date; provided that if a claim notice is delivered in good faith prior to such date, the claim shall survive until finally resolved, and the notifying Party may supplement the notice with additional particularity as information becomes available.

   (c) The running of any survival period with respect to the Sanctions and National Security Representations shall be tolled during the pendency of any investigation, inquiry, or proceeding by a Governmental Authority relating to the subject matter of such representations, from the date the Indemnified Party provides written notice of such investigation, inquiry, or proceeding to the Indemnifying Party until the date that is ninety (90) days after final resolution thereof.

   (d) Notwithstanding any shorter period under applicable Law, the Parties agree that the survival periods set forth herein are contractual limitations periods and supersede any conflicting statute of limitations solely to the extent they lengthen the time to assert a claim as between the Parties.

   Negotiation note:
   "Buyer rejects shortened survival for core/fundamental and sanctions–CFIUS representations. Tiered survival restored: general reps [18] months; Fundamental and Sanctions/National Security Representations through statute of limitations + 60 days, with tolling during government investigations."

================================================================================
IV. CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES AND INTERLOCKS
================================================================================

1. Combined Economic Effect
   Deviations 1 and 3 together reduce both the amount recoverable and the time window for recovery. Even if each were "market" in isolation (they are not, as marked), the package is a material shift of sanctions/CFIUS residual risk to the client. Negotiate as a package; do not trade Cap acceptance for survival concessions without express client authority.

2. NSA–Purchase Agreement Consistency
   Ensure defined terms (Material Adverse Effect, Law, Order, Governmental Authority, Burdensome Condition, Fundamental Representations, Sanctions and National Security Representations) are identical—or expressly cross-incorporated—across the purchase agreement, the NSA, and any side letters. Counterparty MAE carve-outs must not re-enter through a different definitional annex.

3. Disclosure Schedule / Knowledge Qualifiers
   Re-check whether the markup quietly expanded knowledge qualifiers or schedule mechanisms that would further blunt sanctions reps. None were identified in the counterparty summary beyond the three listed deviations; confirm on the face of the full redline before signing off.

4. Silence and Process
   The "silent" Cap reduction warrants a process objection: require a deviation schedule for all numeric and structural changes. Future turns should include a one-page change log.

5. Items Not in Dispute
   Counterparty acceptance of remaining firm-standard provisions should be locked by express statement in the next markup cover note so they are not reopened.

================================================================================
V. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION PACKAGE (SUMMARY)
================================================================================

Item | Counterparty Position | Client Position | Priority
-----|----------------------|-----------------|--------
MAE regulatory carve-outs (CFIUS/sanctions/export) | Carve out of MAE | Reject; keep inside MAE with express inclusion language | CRITICAL
Indemnification Cap | Silently reduced | Restore firm Cap; no silent numeric edits | HIGH
Basket structure | Convert deductible → tipping | Retain deductible; tipping only if Cap increased and threshold cut as a package | HIGH
Special indemnity (sanctions/CFIUS) | At risk of Cap/basket bleed | Outside Cap and Basket; uncapped or Special Cap = Purchase Price | HIGH
Survival of core reps | Shortened limitation period | Tiered survival; Fundamental + Sanctions/NS reps through SoL + 60 days + tolling | HIGH
Other firm-standard provisions | Accepted | Lock as agreed | HOUSEKEEPING

Fallback (only with client authority): limited tipping basket on general claims in exchange for (i) higher Cap, (ii) expressly uncapped sanctions/CFIUS special indemnity, and (iii) full SoL survival on sanctions/CFIUS reps—no compromise on MAE regulatory inclusion.

================================================================================
VI. NEXT STEPS
================================================================================

1. Circulate this memorandum and proposed counter-draft language to the deal team for confirmation of Cap/Basket numbers and survival periods to be inserted in brackets.
2. Prepare the responsive redline of the NSA incorporating Section III counter-draft text and the companion Burdensome Condition / closing-condition alignment.
3. Send a cover issues list to counterparty reflecting the CRITICAL / HIGH dispositions above; request express confirmation that all other firm-standard provisions remain accepted.
4. Re-read the full redline prior to execution to confirm no additional silent deviations beyond the three addressed herein.
5. Coordinate with CFIUS process counsel so that NSA mitigation terms and purchase-agreement MAE / closing conditions remain consistent through Committee engagement.

================================================================================
VII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

The counterparty markup's three deviations—MAE regulatory carve-outs, indemnification Cap reduction with tipping-basket conversion, and shortened survival for core representations—are material and, in a CFIUS National Security Agreement / international trade sanctions setting, risk-allocating against the client on the precise hazards this deal is structured to manage. We recommend rejecting all three as marked, restoring firm-standard economics and risk allocation, and circulating the counter-draft language in Section III as the basis for the next turn.

End of Memorandum.

The memo is risk-prioritized and addresses every counterparty deviation:

1. **CRITICAL — MAE regulatory carve-outs**  
   Rejects carving CFIUS/sanctions/export-control action out of MAE; supplies inclusion language and Burdensome Condition / closing-condition alignment.

2. **HIGH — Indemnification cap + basket**  
   Rejects silent cap
